note: Retronet ICQ cross-list roster — the single source for the contact seeder (scripts/retronet/icq/seed_contacts.py). Each live station carries every OTHER live station + the bot in its contact list. Adding a station is ONE row here, then re-run `seed_contacts.py ssi --apply`. UIN/tier table: docs/lab/retronet/ICQ-ONBOARDING-PLAN.md. uin = the OSCAR screen name: a numeric UIN for the ICQ stations, and an alphanumeric AIM screen name for win311 (Netscape AIM 1.0.414 is an AIM client, not an ICQ one) — rn-tool.py keys the server-side roster by screen name either way. nick = the display name (SSI 0x0131 alias TLV in the server-side roster; also the ICQ directory nickname), never a bare UIN. client = which fallback client-UI seeding driver applies. onboarded=true means LIVE: it gates the SSI cross-list (only live stations appear in each other's rosters). Primary path is SSI/feedbag (`ssi`); the client-UI `seed`/`plan` path is the non-SSI ICQ 2000b fallback. greeter = which greeter instance watches the station: 'icq' (default, HiveBot UIN 10000) or 'aim' (the hivebot AIM screen name, retronet-bot-aim.service). aimScreenName is present ONLY for a station whose client is an AIM client: it is the name that station's own client signs in as, while `uin` is the NUMERIC identity the ICQ fleet addresses it by — held by retronet-aim-bridge, not by the guest. The two exist because AIM refuses an all-numeric screen name and ICQ 2001b silently drops a message from a non-numeric sender, so one account cannot be addressable by both families. `uin` stays the SSI cross-list key either way, so every station carries win311 as a normal contact. See docs/lab/retronet/ICQ-STATION-win311.md.
